audit_rules.generic_id: message_schema.json:13-18 accepts a nonempty string of at most 256 UTF-8 bytes without NUL. It does not specify an owner encoding, printable ASCII, relation grammar, kernel projection or authentic value.
audit_rules.canonical_width: ensure_ascii=true can expand one legal UTF-8 byte such as U+0001 to six canonical ASCII bytes. The generic 256-byte ID limit alone gives a safe 1536-content-byte canonical ceiling, not 256. This does not make arbitrary control-character IDs semantically attainable.
audit_rules.hmac_does_not_define_ids: Frozen HMAC-SHA256 authenticates owner payloads; it does not specify every scalar ID as a digest or token_hex(32).
audit_rules.classification_precedence: The classification is the strongest representation established for the required new field. Historical primitives are identified separately where no frozen new-field mapping adopts them.
audit_rules.existing_primitive_scope: Existing authorization/provider/reflection/runtime owner primitives are recoverable for their own fields only; none supplies the future workspace/preparation/controller relation IDs.
